title: Popescu's theorem reduces to a field as base
statement: Assume that for every field $k$ and every Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with a regular ring map $k\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. Then for all Noetherian rings $R$, $\Lambda$ and every regular ring map $R\to\Lambda$, $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, line 2003), with Situation Tag 07F2 (situation-global: R -> Lambda a regular ring map of Noetherian rings) and the definition of PT after it (Section Tag 07F1); its proof uses More on Algebra Lemma 07C1, Proposition 07CM (proposition-lift), Algebra Lemma 07C3 (lemma-when-colimit), Algebra Lemmas 02LX and 00FR, Lemmas 07F3 (lemma-product), 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), 07CP (lemma-lifting) and 07CT (lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard)

proof.text: Quotients stay in the situation. Say that PT holds for a ring map $R\to\Lambda$ if $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. Let $R\to\Lambda$ be a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $I\subset R$ an ideal. Then $R/I$ and $\Lambda/I\Lambda$ are Noetherian (quotients of Noetherian rings: an ideal of the quotient is the image of an ideal, generated by the images of finitely many generators), $R\to R/I$ is of finite type (generated by no element), so by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change] the base change $R/I\to\Lambda\otimes_RR/I$ is regular, and $\Lambda\otimes_RR/I\cong\Lambda/I\Lambda$ as $R/I$-algebras ($\lambda\otimes\bar r\mapsto\overline{r\lambda}$). So $R/I\to\Lambda/I\Lambda$ is again a regular ring map of Noetherian rings.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), first paragraph ('Note that R/I -> Lambda/I Lambda is another regular ring map of Noetherian rings, see More on Algebra, Lemma 07C1')

proof.text:
Noetherian induction. Assume PT holds for every regular ring map $k	o\Lambda'$ from a field $k$ to a Noetherian ring $\Lambda'$, let $R	o\Lambda$ be a regular ring map of Noetherian rings, and suppose PT fails for it. Let $\mathcal I$ be the set of ideals $I\subset R$ such that PT fails for $R/I	o\Lambda/I\Lambda$; $(0)\in\mathcal I$ since $R/(0)	o\Lambda/(0)\Lambda$ is $R	o\Lambda$. As $R$ is Noetherian, $\mathcal I$ has a maximal element $I$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-ideal-set-maximal]. Put $ ar R=R/I$, $ ar\Lambda=\Lambda/I\Lambda$; by Step 1 $ ar R	o ar\Lambda$ is a regular map of Noetherian rings, PT fails for it, and for every nonzero ideal $ ar J\subset ar R$, $ ar J=J/I$ with $J\supsetneq I$, so $J
otin\mathcal I$ and PT holds for $ ar R/ ar J=R/J	o ar\Lambda/ ar J ar\Lambda=\Lambda/J\Lambda$. Moreover $ ar R
e0$: if $ ar R=0$ then $ ar\Lambda=0$, and PT holds for $0	o0$ (the one-object category with the $0$-algebra $0=0[\,]/(1)$, smooth over $0$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] since it is finitely presented and $H_1(L_{0/0})=0$, $\Omega_{0/0}=0$ are zero modules, is a filtered diagram with colimit $0$). Renaming $ ar R, ar\Lambda$ as $R,\Lambda$, we are in the following situation, which Steps 3-10 show to be contradictory: $R	o\Lambda$ is a regular map of Noetherian rings, $R
e0$, PT fails for $R	o\Lambda$, and PT holds for $R/J	o\Lambda/J\Lambda$ for every nonzero ideal $J\subset R$. Hence $\mathcal I$ is empty for every regular $R	o\Lambda$ of Noetherian rings, in particular $(0)
otin\mathcal I$: PT holds for $R	o\Lambda$, which is the statement.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), first paragraph (the set of ideals I, its maximal element, 'Replacing R by R/I ...')

proof.text: $R$ is reduced. Let $N=\sqrt{(0)}\subset R$ be the nilradical. $N$ is finitely generated ($R$ Noetherian) and $N\subset\sqrt{(0)}$, so $N^t=0$ for some $t\ge1$ [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power]: $N$ is nilpotent. The regular map $R\to\Lambda$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. If $N\neq0$, PT holds for $R/N\to\Lambda/N\Lambda$ by Step 2, so by [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-nilpotent] (with $I=N$) PT holds for $R\to\Lambda$, contradicting Step 2. Hence $N=0$: $R$ is reduced.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), end of first paragraph ('we see by applying Proposition 07CM (proposition-lift) that R is a reduced ring')

proof.text: Reduction to factorizations. Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of $R$-algebras of the form $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/I'$ ($n\ge0$, $I'$ an ideal) that are smooth over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; every smooth $R$-algebra is of finite presentation, hence isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-factorization-criterion-filtered-colimit] PT holds for $R\to\Lambda$ as soon as: (*) for every $R$-algebra $A$ of finite presentation and every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B$ and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $A\to B\to\Lambda$ with composite $\alpha$ (replace $B$ by an isomorphic member of $\mathcal E$). Fix such $A$ and $\alpha$; Steps 5-10 prove (*), which contradicts Step 2.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), second paragraph ('We have to find a factorization A -> B -> Lambda with B smooth over R, see Algebra, Lemma 07C3')

proof.text: PT over the total ring of fractions. Let $S\subset R$ be the set of nonzerodivisors and $Q=S^{-1}R$. $R$ is reduced (Step 3), Noetherian and nonzero, so it has finitely many minimal primes $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], $t\ge1$ (a nonzero ring has a prime, and every prime contains a minimal prime), and by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] each $K_i=R_{\mathfrak q_i}=\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)$ is a field and $Q\to K_1\times\cdots\times K_t$ is an isomorphism. Tensoring with $\Lambda$ over $R$: $S^{-1}\Lambda\cong\Lambda\otimes_RQ\cong\prod_i\Lambda\otimes_RK_i=:\prod_i\Lambda_i$ (localization is base change to $S^{-1}R$, and $\otimes$ commutes with finite products), compatibly with $Q\cong\prod_iK_i$. Each $\Lambda_i=\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is the fibre ring of $R\to\Lambda$ at $\mathfrak q_i$, so it is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)=K_i$ by regularity [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Hence $K_i\to\Lambda_i$ is a regular ring map of Noetherian rings: it is flat, every module over a field being free [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and its only fibre ring, over the prime $(0)$ of $K_i$ with $\kappa((0))=K_i$, is $\Lambda_i\otimes_{K_i}K_i\cong\Lambda_i$. By the hypothesis of the lemma PT holds for each $K_i\to\Lambda_i$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-product], applied $t-1$ times ($(K_1\times\cdots\times K_{s})\times K_{s+1}$ for $s=1,\dots,t-1$), PT holds for $\prod_iK_i\to\prod_i\Lambda_i$, hence, transporting along the isomorphisms $Q\cong\prod_iK_i$, $S^{-1}\Lambda\cong\prod_i\Lambda_i$, for $Q\to S^{-1}\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), third paragraph ('Q = K_1 x ... x K_n is a product of fields, see Algebra, Lemmas 02LX and 00FR. By Lemma 07F3 and our assumption PT holds for S^{-1}R -> S^{-1}Lambda'; the regularity of K_i -> Lambda_i, which Stacks leaves implicit, is written out here)

proof.text: A smooth factorization over $Q$. $S^{-1}A\cong A\otimes_RQ$ is a $Q$-algebra of finite presentation (a presentation of $A$ over $R$ base-changes to one over $Q$), and $S^{-1}\alpha:S^{-1}A\to S^{-1}\Lambda$ is a homomorphism of $Q$-algebras. By Step 5, $S^{-1}\Lambda$ is a colimit, in the category of commutative $Q$-algebras, of a filtered diagram $j\mapsto B_j$ of smooth $Q$-algebras with coprojections $\iota_j$ [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]; by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1) it is also a colimit of the underlying diagram of commutative rings, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] there are $j$ and a $Q$-algebra map $\beta':S^{-1}A\to B_j$ with $\iota_j\circ\beta'=S^{-1}\alpha$. Put $B'=B_j$, $\gamma'=\iota_j$: a factorization $S^{-1}A\to B'\to S^{-1}\Lambda$ of $S^{-1}\alpha$ with $B'$ smooth over $Q=S^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), third paragraph ('Hence we can find a factorization S^{-1}A -> B' -> S^{-1}Lambda with B' smooth over S^{-1}R', i.e. Algebra Lemma 07C3, (1) implies (2))

proof.text: Delocalizing: a strictly standard nonzerodivisor. By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-base] (applied to $R\to A\xrightarrow{\alpha}\Lambda$, $S$ and $S^{-1}A\to B'\to S^{-1}\Lambda$ from Step 6) there are an $R$-algebra $B_0$ of finite presentation, $R$-algebra maps $A\to B_0\to\Lambda$ with composite $\alpha$, and $\pi\in S$ whose image in $B_0$ is elementary standard in $B_0$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. A factorization $B_0\to B\to\Lambda$ with $B$ smooth over $R$ gives the factorization $A\to B_0\to B\to\Lambda$ of $\alpha$ required in (*); so we may replace $(A,\alpha)$ by $(B_0,B_0\to\Lambda)$ and assume that $\pi$ is elementary standard in $A$ over $R$. Then $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$: with the same presentation and $c$, $\pi=a'\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}$ is the sum in Definition 07C7 (2) with $a_{\{1,\dots,c\}}=a'$ and $a_I=0$ for $I\neq\{1,\dots,c\}$, and the second condition is the same [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), fourth paragraph ('We apply Lemma 07F4 ... After replacing A by B we may assume that pi is elementary standard, hence strictly standard in A')

proof.text: Annihilators. $\pi\in S$ is a nonzerodivisor of $R$, hence so is $\pi^k$ for every $k\ge1$, and $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^k)=0$. Since $R\to\Lambda$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], tensoring the injective $R$-linear map $\pi^k:R\to R$ with $\Lambda$ shows that multiplication by $\pi^k$ on $\Lambda$ is injective: $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^k)=0$. So $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^2)$, $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$, $\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^4)=\mathrm{Ann}_R(\pi^8)$ and $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^4)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^8)$ (all zero). Also $\pi^8\ne0$ in $R\ne0$ ($\pi^8\cdot1=0$ would make $1=0$), so $\pi^8R$ is a nonzero ideal.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), fourth paragraph (the annihilator hypotheses of Lemmas 07CP and 07CT, used there without comment)

proof.text: A smooth factorization modulo $\pi^8$ and its lift. By Step 2 PT holds for $R/\pi^8R\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$. $A/\pi^8A=A\otimes_RR/\pi^8R$ is of finite presentation over $R/\pi^8R$ and $\alpha$ induces an $R/\pi^8R$-algebra map $A/\pi^8A\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$; as in Step 6 ([lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1) and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit]) there is a factorization $A/\pi^8A\to\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$ with $\bar C$ a smooth, in particular finitely presented, $R/\pi^8R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lifting] with $\pi^4$ in place of $\pi$ ($R$ Noetherian, the annihilator conditions by Step 8, and $R/\pi^8R\to\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda$): there are an $R$-algebra $D$ of finite presentation, an $R$-algebra map $D\to\Lambda$ and an $R$-algebra map $\bar C\to D/\pi^4D$ making the diagram of that lemma commute, with properties (a)-(d). $R\to D$ is smooth at every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $D$ (in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]): if $\pi\notin\mathfrak q$ by (b) ($\pi^4\notin\mathfrak q$); if $\pi\in\mathfrak q$, then $\mathfrak q\supset\pi^4D$ defines a prime of $D/\pi^4D$, whose inverse image in $\bar C$ is a prime at which $R/\pi^8R\to\bar C$ is smooth (it is smooth everywhere: $\bar C_1=\bar C$ is smooth), so (c) applies. The composite $A/\pi^8A\to\bar C\to D/\pi^4D$ kills $\pi^4$, so it factors through an $R$-algebra map $A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$; by commutativity of the diagram of the lemma (right square) its composite with $D/\pi^4D\to\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ equals $A/\pi^8A\to\bar C\to\Lambda/\pi^8\Lambda\to\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$, i.e. the map induced by $\alpha$: the map $A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$ is compatible with the maps to $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field, lines 2011-2064), fourth paragraph ('We know that R/pi^8R -> Lambda/pi^8Lambda satisfies PT. Hence we can find a factorization ... By Lemma 07CP (lemma-lifting) we can find an R-algebra map D -> Lambda with D smooth over R and a factorization R/pi^4R -> A/pi^4A -> D/pi^4D -> Lambda/pi^4Lambda'; Stacks applies the lemma with pi^4 for pi)

proof.text: Desingularization and the final solve. By Step 9, $H_{D/R}=D$: for each prime $\mathfrak q$ of $D$ there is $g\notin\mathfrak q$ with $D_g$ smooth over $R$, so the set $G$ of such $g$ lies in no prime, $(G)=D$ and $H_{D/R}=\sqrt{(G)}=D$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-desingularize-strictly-standard] to $R$, $\Lambda$, $\pi$ (annihilator conditions by Step 8), $A\to\Lambda$, $D\to\Lambda$ ($A$, $D$ of finite presentation), $\pi$ strictly standard in $A$ (Step 7) and the compatible map $A/\pi^4A\to D/\pi^4D$ (Step 9): there are an $R$-algebra $B$ of finite presentation and $R$-algebra maps $A\to B\to\Lambda$, $D\to B$ compatible with the maps to $\Lambda$, with $B=H_{D/R}B\subset H_{B/R}$; so $H_{B/R}=B$ and $H_{B/R}\Lambda=\Lambda$. By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-final-solve] there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B''$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $R$-algebra maps $B\to B''\to\Lambda$ with composite $B\to\Lambda$. Then $A\to B\to B''\to\Lambda$ has composite $\alpha$, which proves (*) of Step 4; so PT holds for $R\to\Lambda$, contradicting Step 2. (Stacks concludes directly that $B$ is smooth over $R$, $H_{B/R}=B$ meaning that $R\to B$ is smooth at every prime; the final solve gives the factorization without that local-to-global step.)

split_report.summary: Wrote the proof of Stacks Lemma 07F5 (smoothing.tex lines 2011-2064) in ten steps following its four paragraphs: regular base change to R/I (07C1, existing), Noetherian induction on the set of ideals where PT fails (existing Mathlib leaf for maximal elements; the zero ring case written out), reducedness via nilpotence of the nilradical (existing leaf fg-ideal-radical-power) and Proposition 07CM (new node), the factorization criterion (07C3, existing), PT over the total ring of fractions as a product of fields (02LX with 00EW/00EU/00FR, new node; regularity of K_i -> Lambda_i written out from the fibre ring at a minimal prime; 07F3 new node), the smooth factorization over Q (07C3 (1)=>(2), existing nodes), delocalization (07F4, new node; definition 07C7 of elementary/strictly standard elements, new node), annihilator conditions from flatness (elementary), the lift modulo pi^8 by Lemma 07CP (new node) with pi^4 for pi, and the desingularization 07CT (new node) followed by the existing final-solve node 07EU in place of Stacks' implicit 'H_{B/R} = B implies B smooth'. Statement and stmt_deps unchanged; all tags checked against tags/tags (proposition-lift = 07CM, lemma-lifting = 07CP, lemma-desingularize-strictly-standard = 07CT).

reviewed.note: Reviewed by the lead (opus-relaunch6). Ten steps along Stacks 07F5 (smoothing.tex 2011-2064), split by one level with seven new unsplit nodes (tags verified: 07C7 strictly standard elements, 07F3 product, 07F4 delocalize-base, 07CM lift along nilpotent ideals, 07CP lifting, 07CT desingularize strictly standard, 02LX total ring of fractions of a reduced Noetherian ring): base change along quotients (07C1), Noetherian induction (zero ring written out), R reduced (07CM), factorization criterion 07C3, PT over Q = prod K_i (regularity of K_i -> Lambda_i written out, 07F3 stated without the Situation 07F2 hypotheses it does not use), smooth factorization over Q, delocalization with a strictly standard nonzerodivisor pi, annihilators (elementary), lifting modulo pi^8 by 07CP, 07CT then H_{B/R} = B and the final solve node (07EU) instead of a 'smooth at every prime => smooth' node (acceptable, below the unit). No cycle with popescu-final-solve.
